Estimate a Gaussian graphical model with the EBIC graphical lasso

Source: R/glasso.R
ebic_glasso.Rd

ebic_glasso() estimates a Gaussian graphical model: a network in which variables are nodes joined by partial correlations, and a missing edge means two variables are independent given all the others. It fits the graphical lasso, which shrinks weak partial correlations to zero, and chooses the penalty by the extended Bayesian information criterion (Epskamp & Fried, 2018).

An edge is the association between two variables after controlling for all other variables in the network. The penalty sets weak partial correlations to exactly zero, so that only the associations supported by the data are retained, and the EBIC balances the fit of the model against the number of edges. ebic_glasso() fits the graphical lasso over a sequence of penalties, selects the penalty with the lowest EBIC and returns the partial-correlation network at that penalty. It takes raw data, or a correlation matrix together with its sample size. gamma sets how strongly the EBIC favours sparse networks, refit = "unregularized" keeps the selected edges but estimates them without shrinkage, and threshold removes weak edges after estimation.

The returned network is the optimum of the penalized likelihood at the selected penalty, which certificate() checks.

This regularized partial-correlation network is the standard estimator for continuous and ordinal data in psychological network analysis. For data far from normality, huge_network() fits the same model after a rank-based transformation. ggm_modselect() selects an unregularized network by stepwise search, pcor_network() keeps every partial correlation, and ising_fit() and mgm_fit() estimate networks of binary and mixed variables. The model is the one fitted by qgraph::EBICglasso().

Usage

ebic_glasso(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  gamma = 0.5,
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.01,
  threshold = 0,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  native = TRUE,
  lambda_path = NULL,
  penalize_diagonal = FALSE,
  refit = TRUE,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix. It must be symmetric and positive semi-definite. n is then required.

n

Sample size, required with cor_matrix: a single finite number= 1. Ignored when data is given.

gamma

EBIC hyperparameter, a number >= 0; larger values favour sparser networks and 0 gives the ordinary BIC. Default 0.5.

nlambda

Number of penalties scanned, a whole number >= 2. Default 100.

lambda_min_ratio

Smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest, in (0, 1). Default 0.01.

threshold

Absolute partial correlation below which an edge is set to zero after estimation: a single number >= 0. Default 0. A logical value (the threshold = TRUE rule of qgraph) is refused. A positive value leaves the certificate missing.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) uses pairwise-complete correlations adjusted to the nearest positive-definite matrix; "listwise" drops incomplete rows. The two agree for complete data.

native

TRUE (default) uses the package's own solver. FALSE solves each penalty with the glasso package, which must be installed, to reproduce results of the glasso and qgraph packages.

lambda_path

Optional numeric vector of positive penalties to scan, in the given order, replacing nlambda and lambda_min_ratio. Useful when resampling: the path of the full data, reused for every resample, keeps the selected penalties comparable. Default NULL.

penalize_diagonal

Whether the penalty also applies to the diagonal of the precision matrix. Default FALSE.

refit

What to return at the selected penalty: TRUE (default) the optimum at that penalty; FALSE the fit obtained while scanning the penalties, less precise and kept to reproduce earlier results; "unregularized" the unpenalized maximum-likelihood network restricted to the selected edges, without shrinkage.

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network (the columns left after non-numeric and constant columns are dropped).

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are partial correlations. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; print() shows the selected penalty and the certificate; certificate() reports the check. The object also stores the precision matrix (precision), the selected penalty (lambda), gamma, the correlation matrix used (cor_matrix), the EBIC of the selected network (ebic), the penalties scanned and their EBIC (lambda_path, ebic_path) and, with refit = "unregularized", the selected graph (support). Nodes keep the column order of the input.

Details

For a precision matrix \(\Theta\) with \(E\) nonzero off-diagonal entries, fitted to a correlation matrix \(S\) of \(p\) variables and \(n\) observations, the criterion is $$\mathrm{EBIC} = -2L + E \log n + 4 \gamma E \log p, \quad L = \frac{n}{2}\left(\log\det\Theta - \mathrm{tr}(S\Theta)\right).$$ The penalties form a log-spaced sequence of nlambda values from the largest absolute off-diagonal correlation, at which the network is empty, down to lambda_min_ratio times that value. When two penalties give the same EBIC, the one earlier in the path is selected, which on the default path is the larger penalty and the sparser network. Unless lambda_path is given, a correlation matrix with no off-diagonal association returns the empty network with penalty 0.

With na_method = "pairwise" and incomplete data, the sample size entering the EBIC is the median number of observations available for a pair of variables.

The certificate is computed by glasso_kkt(). With refit = "unregularized" the network is no longer a penalized optimum and is checked by ggm_support_kkt() instead. With refit = FALSE or native = FALSE the network is solved to a looser tolerance, and its certificate can exceed the default tolerance of certificate(). After a positive threshold the certificate is missing; print() still shows the value for the network before thresholding.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when an argument is out of range, threshold is logical, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, n is missing with cor_matrix, data has fewer than two usable variables, a pair of variables is never observed together, labels do not match the nodes, native = FALSE without the glasso package, or every penalty fails to fit; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped. A psychnet_dropped_columns message names non-numeric columns that were dropped.

References

Friedman, J., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2008). Sparse inverse covariance estimation with the graphical lasso. Biostatistics, 9(3), 432-441. doi:10.1093/biostatistics/kxm045

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604-612.

Epskamp, S., & Fried, E. I. (2018). A tutorial on regularized partial correlation networks. Psychological Methods, 23(4), 617-634. doi:10.1037/met0000167

See also

certificate() and glasso_kkt() for the check; huge_network(), ggm_modselect() and pcor_network() for related Gaussian networks; psychnet(), which routes method = "glasso" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:6, 1:6, "-"))
fit <- ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 250)
fit
#> <psychnet> glasso network
#>   nodes: 6   edges: 5   (undirected)
#>   lambda: 0.004   gamma: 0.5
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.10e-10
as.data.frame(fit)
#>   from to    weight
#> 1   V1 V2 0.3681824
#> 2   V2 V3 0.3423189
#> 3   V3 V4 0.3423189
#> 4   V4 V5 0.3423189
#> 5   V5 V6 0.3681824
certificate(fit)
#>   method certificate kind certified
#> 1 glasso 1.10463e-10  kkt      TRUE
